stdout: (no config - demo: two invented products; one stale fact, one unanswered blocker, no disqualifiers)
AAJ - BATTLECARD: Ledgerline vs Tallybook
FIX BEFORE SHARING - 2 issues would cost a rep credibility in front of a buyer. Fix those first.
Record: won 7 of 12 decided deals (58%; plausibly 36% to 78%)
WHERE WE WIN
- Month-end close in days, not weeks, for multi-entity finance teams
proof: Named reference customer with a before-and-after close time, approved for use
- Setup without a consultant
proof: Onboarding times from our own CRM records, available on request
WHERE THEY WIN (be honest)
- Larger app marketplace
then: Ask which integrations they actually use; we cover the common accounting and payroll ones.
- Lower entry price for a single entity
QUESTIONS TO ASK
- How long does month-end close take you today, and which step takes longest?
- How many entities do you expect to run in a year
OBJECTIONS
- "Tallybook is cheaper" (misunderstanding)
acknowledge: For one entity, their entry plan does cost less than ours.
reframe:     The comparison that matters is the cost once you add the second and third entity you mentioned.
prove:       Walk through their public per-entity pricing against ours for their entity count.
- "We need an app we already use" (blocker)
acknowledge: Fair.
reframe:     -
prove:       -
FACTS (sourced, dated)
- Their multi-entity plan is priced per entity  [their public pricing page, 2026-04-02]
BEFORE SHARING
!  "Their multi-entity plan is priced per entity" was last checked 177 days ago. Re-check it before a rep uses it - this engine flags anything older than 90 days.
!  "We need an app we already use" is missing reframe, prove. Each response needs all three: agree with what is true, change the frame, then show evidence.
-  "Lower entry price for a single entity" is acknowledged with nothing after it. Add when it matters less for this buyer, so the rep has somewhere to go.
-  The acknowledge step for "We need an app we already use" is very short. A slogan is not an answer a rep can say out loud.
-  There is a real blocker but no disqualifier. Some blockers mean the deal is the wrong fit - say when to walk rather than overcome.
-  "How many entities do you expect to run in a year" is not phrased as a question.
-  No disqualifiers. Name the situations where the rival is the better fit and the rep should walk away.
